text: It's time to update my review. I can't believe it's been three years. And this place has done nothing but get better with age. The seating has improved, the floor now supports the dancing they host on weekends, and the general ambiance has improved. But it's still a Puerto Rican restaurant, so it retains a certain charm that your typical chain restaurant can't touch. And the food.... I have to make the disclaimer that I'm Puerto Rican. So when it comes to Puerto Rican food, I'm an expert. I know good Puerto Rican food. And and I know bad and mediocre food. I can unequivocally state this is freaking outstanding Puerto Rican food. In Tampa it just doesn't get any better than this. The taste remains home made. Maintaining that taste in a commercial venture is hard. If you want to taste authentic Puerto Rican food, look no further. Ask for "morcilla". It's blood sausage. Don't Google it. You don't want to know what's in it or how it's made. Trust me. But if you like sausage, you will love this. Just bit into in and don't think too much about it. Ask for "alcapurrias". It's Puerto Rican fried appetizers that are amazingly delicious. They make them in house. It's the real deal. And, of course, there's the mofongo. It's the house specialty. I don't remember having it better even in Puerto Rico. Bring a big empty stomach. You're gonna need it. I eat out all over Tampa Bay and enjoy all sorts of food. I prefer genuine ethnic foods as they tend to be more flavorful and interesting. But I have a soft spot for Puerto Rican food, and I'm glad there is one place in Tampa where I can get the authentic experience without having to go back to the island. Come and enjoy this place. It's as good as it gets.

Being at though we arrived at 10:35 and the kitchen closed at 10:45(so we were told) there was only a late night limited menu being served with three things to choose from. When we first arrived one of the servers explained since it was so late we needed to sit at the bar. However, that was false because two groups that arrived after us were seated. This had me heated because I would rather not have sat at the bar, sine the game was on and I have no desire to watch it. Nor sit there and act interested with people who really were, lol. After sitting at the bar I order a drink, the drink was mediocre and kind of watered down. The bartender at first seemed uninterested to serve me. Until I kind of killed her with kindness then she was more friendly. After pushing the drink to the side I decided to order the Jerk chicken, rice an beans and cabbage. Everything was pretty tasty. The jerk chicken was superrrr spicy, but for sure delicious. text: I've been to Angeline a few times now, and each time has been amazing! The space has been lightened up quite a bit since its days as Stella, and for the better in my opinion. Here's a few highlights I want to share with everyone: -the sherry menu! Honestly, the best in the city. Probably the most expansive as well. If sherry is your thing, you NEED to come check this place out. -The cocktail menu: there's a cocktail with tequila and beet juice and somehow it doesn't taste anything like a Cinco de Mayo borscht. It's amazing. All the drinks are. (Believe me, I've drank most of them :) ) -The roasted cauliflower: even if you're just stopping in for a cocktail, this is worth ordering as a bar snack. It's AMAZING. So much flavor, and the texture is heavenly. A few other things: Angeline started doing brunch recently, and while I haven't tried it yet, I have read the menu and I can't wait to check it out. If it's a nice night, check out the patio for dinner. It's in such a beautiful, quiet spot, you'll forget the craziness of the French Market is just around the corner. There's even an herb-fountain where all the basil, rosemary, etc. for the kitchen are grown!

text: My girlfriend Elizabeth's Mom and brother told us about this place as soon as we got to Tampa on our last visit. It sounded right up my alley, so I was looking forward to trying it. When we came in, the first thing I noticed was that the decor was that of a hipster coffee shop. There was art for sale on the walls, and lots of hipster looking people on couches. I'm not a huge fan of that culture to be honest. However, seeing hipsters somewhere is usually a good sign. They seem to have good taste when it comes to food! I tried every single flavor until I could tell that I was making the worker uncomfortable. (I probably tried 10 different flavors.) I settled on chocolate habanero and peanut butter in a waffle cone bowl. * I figured that this would be a good combo, and my god.... it was probably the best ice cream I've ever had. The chocolate habanero, which I really only got because it sounded interesting, was actually pretty awesome. The peanut butter flavored ice cream will probably stick with me as a life long memory. *A little background on my decision to try this flavor. So, I have this rule that if something sounds like a really weird combination of things, it's probably good. I mean, you can't exactly combine to random things if people didn't LOVE the end result. They would have to take it off the menu. I've found this to be an excellent rule of thumb for trying new things.

text: If you want a quick removal of surface dirt go for it. I had my car washed with their "hot wax" option. Spent $20 only to find my front window still dirty. I mentioned this to the individuals drying and I was told I had to ask them to power spray my truck before going through the car wash (which was done). One of the attendants says if I had a problem I needed to go around and through again. I then called and was told that they should have prepped my truck better and that they only do rewashes the same day. I informed the attendant and the individual over the phone that I was not asking for a rewash and did not have the time to sit in line to have it done again. Since then I received an email from the owner challenging me to come in for a rewash on a subsequent day. He informed me that he doesn't know of a car wash that would offer that and that he didn't understand why I didn't just go back through the car wash. I won't harp on the sarcastic undertone of his email but suffice to say I was surprised I was hearing from the owner. Allow me to elaborate. I informed the gentlemen I spoke to on the phone that I was on my way to an event and did not have time to go through the line to get my truck washed again. Furthermore, while other car washes may not offer rewashes after the same day, I have honestly not had a need for a rewash on my vehicle. Lastly, as the manager of a business, one cannot express appreciation for feedback and then through sarcasm and a challenging demeanor attempt to offer rebuttals for the feedback. The root of my concern was (per my phone call) informing you that my car was still dirty and to express my concern over the attitude and demeanor of one of your employees. That's it. I did not want a rewash but simply assurance that in the future you would try to do better. I will refrain from recommending another business as I do not want my review removed as it was before. Suffice it to say I will respectfully decline the sarcastic offer to rewash my truck and will continue to go to a different location for car wash services.

text: On 3/28/15 I purchased a refrigerator from Clark's appliance auction. I hired Here to There Movers to move the item the next day. They told me they would be done by 10 am and would start at my house with my delivery. I did not receive the item until 5 pm. He did not have time to look up the replacement part, so I emailed him with item number and cost to replace the damaged panel. I followed up on 4/15, 4/17, and 4/24 and received no response on my claim. On 4/29 I was told they would pay out their minimum coverage amount. He reiterated they would pay out the minimum coverage that they offer on their contract. I told him that my biggest issue was that they did not offer me the higher coverage, and that I felt it was a shady business practice in an effort for them to keep their insurance claims down. I told him that I found it to be a massive lack of integrity on the part of the company to not offer the higher insurance coverage, and then lie about it - he disagreed and refused to budge on the payout. text: $12.00 for the museum and $5.00 for the rooftop. Go early in the weekend so you can park in the City Museum parking lot for five dollars. If you get there after 11 o'clock in the morning you may not be able to find a parking spot. Go early and pack a lunch. Because after you purchase your wristband you can leave the city Museum and come back in. We are in frugal family so instead of paying four dollars for a hotdog and $2.98 for a soda we ate our lunches outside that we had stored in the vehicle. Also going early gives you the benefit of being able to explore the place without being pressured by a large group of people. Go to the rooftop for everyone filters into it towards the end of the day. With your five dollar fee you can ride the Ferris wheel for free. Early on when you're done with the rooftop go down to the case. That area can be very congested and you can lose a little one pretty quick. I have to give kudos to the designers of the museum. They did make it to where children can go into a lot of nooks and crannies but still funnel into an area easily accessed by adults. Sometimes they just call around in a big circle and come right back to you ( you will know what I mean when you go there). Do yourself a favor and wear comfortable clothing to include tennis shoes. There are a lot of surface areas to climb on nothing is more comfortable than wearing restrictive clothing and sandals. I also saw a lot of parents that brought knee pads. Are your their visit the world aquarium on the second floor. They have lots of exotic animals for you to see for only $7.95.

text: Finch and Fork has really evolved into an essential part of Santa Barbara fine dining scene since James Siao took over the kitchen. It is much better than the typical hotel restaurant. Service is good, the atmosphere is comfortable, the bar turns out high quality cocktails, and the food is always delectable. I had dinner here on Friday and enjoyed the whole experience. Thick hearty pork chop was grilled to medium doneness so it was juicy and tender, paired with sweet butternut puree, and warm spicy ginger flavor crumbles. Dry packed scallops were seared to a silky medium rare, placed on top of corn salsa and guacamole, further enhanced with grapefruit sections and chorizo vinaigrette. The salt and pepper chicken wings could use a little more salt. The glaze was the same as the glaze in pork ribs and pickled watermelon dish (available during the summer months), sweet, spicy, and savory. A few pieces of pickled celery cuts through the greasiness of fried food. The mac and cheese was made with mornay sauce and bacon, topped with extra cheese so it baked up crunchy and bubbling. My favorite dessert is the toasted banana shake, this and the budino from Olio are two of my favorite desserts in Santa Barbara. The only miss of the night was the sticky toffee cake. It was dry as if it was heated a few minutes too long. The menu changes with season. I have had the pork cheek with gnocchi, grilled ribs with pickled watermelon, sunchoke smear with smoked salmon, and grilled steak with chimichurri sauce. They were all delicious and the only less than stellar dish I had here was the halibut in a mountain of frisee, which was axed from the menu and hadn't returned since the early days of Finch and Fork.

text: Beware of this place. DO NOT SIGN ANYTHING UNLESS YOU ARE SURE OF WHAT YOU SIGN. It has been years since our court hearing but it seems that a month or so doesn't go by with me not hearing yet another horrible story about the way Bill Pearce does business. Instead of sharing a story I just heard yesterday, I will share my own even though it is outdated. I custom ordered a 330xi and leased it for 3 years....at the end of the lease the sales guy and the GM really tried hard to get me to buy out my lease or custom order a whole new car as I wanted the 335xi of which they had none on their lot. After 5 hours of going back and forth, they talked me in to ordering a custom 335xi of which we had no vin # and/or the car wasn't even in the making. Their was NO contract to sign as their was no vin # yet. They had me sign my name on a BLANK sheet of paper. I called 12 hours later(after sleeping on it) and asked the salesman to cancel the whole deal. He wasn't happy and said he would have to talk to his GM about it and call me back. He did call and I kept refusing to go through with the deal and definitely was NOT going to sign anything else. A few weeks went by and as I was leaving my garage 1 day, I got served with a 10 day notice to pay a fine for $2,500 for cancellation. I did not pay and so we went to court. The judge could not decide what to do(I have heard he drives a BMW) and told both parties he would decide in a month or so. I got the letter and the judge said since I signed my name that I had some responsibility and reduced my fine to $1,000. I then found out ALL of this was against the laws of DMV. I was unaware that the DMV have their own laws and actual police. I called DMV and a really nice officer came to my house. I showed him the blank sheet of paper with my signature on it and he was furious that this even made it in to the court room. He then went to Bill Pearce and demanded to see my paperwork and the GM was uncooperative. The officer then demanded the owner to get to the dealership so they could talk. The owner was uncooperative and the officer gave them 15 minutes to produce my blank sheet of paper or he was closing the business down(I was so happy to hear this as finally some justice:-)))!!!). Anyhow, I was given the name of an attorney that handles suing dealerships for shady practice and so I hired him to appeal the judges decision. He made 1 call to Bill Pearce attorney and the case was closed and I never did pay them. HOWEVER, I did go through the 1 1/2 of stress and many phone calls, meetings, court etc... and did have to pay the attorney $250.00 for the call that put a STOP to all of the b.s. These jerks actually went through with the $60,000 custom order which I have heard sat on their lot for over 2 years. I guess they did get their bad Karma/Carma. in the end....hehe.... Please read ALL of these reviews as I am now on my 4th 330xi and definitely do not mind driving to Sac to do business. Niello is awesome and if you love the car like I do, don't let these jerks influence what kind of car you drive. Yes, if you are under warranty you will have to drive over the hill once a year or so for service. I now make special plans when going to Niello and go to the city or Napa or something fun.....I hate to read some of these reviews and see that people feel forced to choose another type of car just to avoid dealing with Bill Pearce. text: So, I bought a house last year (yay!). And, then I realized I needed to fill it (boo?). For the majority of my time I work from home (yay!). But sitting on the couch/kitchen table just was not conducive to the space I now had (boo?). Since I am without kids for now, I had a bedroom with big windows, a window seat, wonderful light, and fantastic views to use as an office. I have a fancy printer, briefcase, diplomas, fancy rug, and all other sort of office things. I just needed a big ol' desk and a modern, ergonomic chair. First stop was Office Depot on/in West End. The manager, Mindy, took great care of me and I found both the heavy, austere, dark wood desk I wanted as well as the modern ergonomic chair I needed to make sure my Mr. Burns-like posture was held at bay for as long as possible. Thing is, this stuff is big, heavy and comes in pieces. What to do? Delivery and assembly. The delivery part of the tale was a nightmare. Courier Express was a complete disaster: late, argumentative, disagreeable, and threw my heavy boxes into my (open) doorway and kept it moving. The whole point of delivery was having them deliver to where I needed the furniture set up. Didn't happen. Phone calls to their office/warehouse was about as effective as the Cubs in September.* Vowing a fatwa, I managed to figure out a way to carry the crazy heavy pieces through the ground floor, up the stairs and to my office. And then I waited for assembly. I was a bit scared. I shouldn't have been. My guy was on time, polite, came with all his tools, and was ready to get to work. I posted up downstairs and let him have at it. In no time at all, I had an office chair that suited me to a tee (I'm sitting in it now). It seems like a small thing but it was so gratifying to finally have. Then came time for leviathan. This desk was no joke but as I listened to hammering, drills and the like, before I knew it, I had a large, stately desk that is going to serve me well for many years to come. I was extremely impressed with the speed with which he worked. I offered water but he had his own. This guy was good. AND, he put all the mess back in the boxes which significantly cut down on my clean up. I would use ARS again and again for my big furniture assembly projects. Why do it yourself when you can pay a pro to do it better than you could? *I got my money back for the (non)service.

text: DO NOT BUY A USED CAR FROM THEM WITHOUT TAKING IT TO A MECHANIC FIRST. I purchased a used car from them, a clean looking 2002 model with 85,000 miles. I offered them the sticker price out the door. The salesmen comes back and says you can have the car for less, but without a warranty. I agree and see a slight smile creep across his face. I should have known better. I drive it home from the dealership, it drives fine. I get back in several hours later, and the check engine light comes on. I take it to my mechanic, who codes it out for a misfire on #4, and a stater misfire. He does a tune-up (new coil, plugs, filter, L.O.F, etc) and the light goes off. I drive it again, the light comes back on. I take it back to my mechanic, and it's the same misfire issues (it's most likely a computer issue), after all the work. This all happened within 4 days of the purchase. Basically, the dealership accepted this vehicle, knowing that there was an issue, and their service team did the work to turn off the light, and keep it off. There's no way it was some coincidence. It's my dumb fault for trusting a car dealer. Don't buy a used car from these scumbags without taking it to a mechanic first, to see when the last time the check engine light was on. I am confident they knew that this was going to be an issue, so basically it's fraud. Stay away.

text: This place is so bad it feels like a lost Chappelle Show skit--what would a wine shop be like if Deebo worked the register. I mean, I'm basically a socialist, and this place makes me extol the virtues of private enterprise. The selection is terrible, and the workers are uniformly rude, unprofessional, unhelpful, and just generally awful. I've been going to this and other West Philly PA Wine & Spirits stores for about five years now (this one hasn't been open that long), and in that time, not a single employee has ever greeted me or asked me if they could help me, let alone made a recommendation. And they work in a god damn service industry! To get a sense of just how much of a failure the PA Wine & Liquor system is, first go to this store, then walk about four blocks over to the privately owned (beer) Bottle Shop at Local 44. And the service at Local 44 isn't stellar, but compared to the wine & liquor store, it's like being waited on by fucking Spratt from Downton Abbey (incidentally, a Spratt/Deebo buddy flick is long overdue). What's maddening about the whole thing is that there's no reason it needs to be so terrible. You don't need an advanced degree to be friendly, polite, and knowledgeable about wine/liquor. You just need to have basic social skills and give a fuck about the industry you're working in (shit, with public libraries, you don't even need money or an internet connection to learn about wine). Apart from the appalling disservice these stores (and this store in particular) do to the PA public, they arguably do an even greater disservice to their employees. Because eventually (and I suspect sooner rather than later), there's going to be a referendum on privatizing these stores, and with all of their experience working in the wine/liquor business, these employees OUGHT to be first in line to open their own stores or be hired to help run a store. But the idea that a private wine shop would ever hire these employees is, unfortunately, laughable. And that's a huge fucking disservice to the employees, who will be left unemployed once privitization occurs, and all their 'experience' will count for nothing. If these stores can't make a very quick, very radical improvement in selection and service, they need to be done away with.

text: DO NOT LET THIS COMPANY INTO YOUR HOME. If you have no other choice and have to, then ABSOLUTELY DO NOT LEAVE THEM UNATTENDED NEAR YOUR HVAC SYSTEM. I will never use this company again, and I would strongly urge others to find a different HVAC Company. My house has 2 zones for upstairs and downstairs. In July of 2013 I had to replace the downstairs HVAC system. I used Christian HVAC for that job because they were recommended to me. $4,000.00 later they installed a new outdoor Carrier AC unit, and retro-fitted the internal Trane Air Handler. (My internal unit was designed for the old R22 Freon, so I needed a new AC Coil on the inside air handler to work with the new outdoor Carrier unit that runs on Puron.) This past Thursday I had a problem with the downstairs HVAC unit they installed. Around 4:00 the house felt warm so I tried to lower the temp, and the outdoor unit was running, but the internal air handler was not. I checked unit and noticed my Freon line was ice cold to the touch, so in a panic and without anyone else to call I reached out to my Christian HVAC salesperson. I was going to call him soon to get pricing on replacing my other HVAC units, but that sure isn't going to happen now. He called me back and had me check a few things to troubleshoot the problem, the first thing he me check was if the unit was draining water because if the drain gets clogged water can back up into and freeze the system. I snaked drain cleared clog, but with the iced up Freon line he suggested I have a maintenance tech come out. I got a call from their Dispatcher and got on the schedule for next day, and was told turn the AC off and to switch fan to the "On" position to put system into De-Frost mode. I ran the De-Frost for 4 hours, and at 12am the Freon line was no longer iced up so I turned the AC back on and it started cooling the house. Next morning, I checked again and nothing was iced up and the first floor was cool, so I thought the problem was fixed. My salesperson called, and asked whether I wanted the service appointment or not. I said yes. We then agreed that he would call me the next morning to set up a time to come by and give me pricing for the new units that I have to replace. In hindsight he sounded reluctant for me to have the service appointment, maybe he knew what could happen. Their tech arrived and I took him to units and I explained the history of the last 24 hours. Again, once the system finished the De-Frost process the unit was functioning fine and my first floor was cool. What happened next was unbelievable - after the tech took the panels off the unit he asked me to lower the temperature so we could hear the system kick on. Trusting person that I am, I left him in front of my units for 2 minutes while I went to first floor thermostat and lowered the temperature. I went back to basement, and the tech told me that the unit's "Control Board" is fried and it will be a $550.00 repair job. I cannot shake the suspicion that the tech in some way sabotaged my unit while I was away. The unit was working fine before he arrived. The part that was installed can be purchased online for $120.00, and it took the tech maybe a 1/2 hour to install it. I griped about the price and was put on the phone with Dan Jr. who more or less intimidated me into having the work performed. I told him about needing to have my other units replaced, and he then gave me a 20% discount on the job. "Great 440.00 is better than $550.00" I thought, but after I hung up the phone the tech then asked me about what Dan said to do regarding the "Service Fee". So I got back on the phone with Dan and was told I had to pay $89.00 for the diagnostic work the tech performed to "determine the problem with my unit". So I basically paid the $550.00 - $440.00 for the part and 1/2 hour install, and $90.00 for the tech to sabotage my system. Finally, and I think that this more than anything proves I was taken, but I never got a call today from the salesperson about coming to give me pricing to replace the other HVAC units in my house. I will never use this company again, and if I were you I would pass this review along to your friends and family so they are aware of how this company conducts business. And, if I were a new agency I would try to set up a sting operation to catch these guys in their business practices. I will state again that my review is based upon my perception of how the events unfolded. I am not stating for a fact that the above happened, but I am a pretty handy guy and posses some knowledge about home repair work. Again, my AC unit was working fine until I left the tech in front of the system unattended - do not let them into your home and if you must do not leave them unattended!!!

text: I agree that the wait is intolerable at this branch. However, what our local elected representatives do not realize is the horrible post office service affects employment for local residents. Most businesses will move to a location where they can more easily send and receive mail, and take the jobs with them. Furthermore, this is a prime example of why the postal service desks (but not the entire post office) should be privatized. Rather than maintain this inefficient branch, simply allow a local bank or another local business to set up a counter to handle the U.S. mail. If they do not provide good customer service then do not renew the contract with that private company. The government's arguments against privatization are not that persuasive. Sure the post office houses valuable items, but so does the local bank, and the inventory at the local Home Depot, or the local FEDEX dropoff location is probably more valuable than the inventory at the post office. The other argument against it, that the post office would have to pick up mail from too many locations, is not persuasive either. How many streetside post office mailboxes are visited each day? In today's world it would not be impossible to allow a local establishment to tap into the post office computer system. We let local businesses sell lottery tickets and that computer system is pretty sophisticated. Oh, and did I mention that we've privatized some of our country's military operations? Hopefully some day the government will realize that privatization of postal service counters is the way to go, so we can make the post office relevant again. It should become so good that Amazon does not feel the need to test drone delivery of purchases.
